I am 48 years old and have been farming since I was a teenager. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land here in Quzhou. I finished middle school, so I can read seed labels and follow the county's technical guidance, but I am not one for complicated new methods. I stick with what works.

This year, as every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on my main 7 mu plot. The wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October with an improved variety I bought from the local supply store. It is a reliable variety that yields about 1,000 jin per mu if the weather cooperates. I rotary-tilled before sowing to break up the soil and bury the maize stubble from last summer. For the wheat, I will irrigate three times: once in late winter if it is dry, and twice in spring — at jointing and at heading. I apply fertilizer in two rounds — a basal compound dressing at sowing and a urea topdressing in spring — totaling about 50 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag. I will spray pesticides four times, mainly for aphids and rust, and for weeds.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid summer maize on the same 7 mu. There is no time to waste — the heat arrives fast — so I will plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble using the seeder. The hybrid maize gives me about 1,100 jin per mu. I irrigate twice, once at the jointing stage and once at filling, and I apply compound fertilizer at planting. I spray three times for borers and weeds. No-tillage saves me time and diesel, and the stubble helps keep moisture.

On my remaining 3 mu, I will grow cotton. It brings in cash that wheat and maize do not, and the price has been decent. I rotary-till in spring, plant a hybrid cotton variety, irrigate twice, and fertilize lightly. Cotton needs many pesticide sprays — I will spray about 14 times through the season to control bollworms and aphids — but my wife and I can manage it. I expect about 550 jin per mu of seed cotton.

This is my plan. I do not gamble with new crops. Wheat and maize feed my family and the cotton gives us spending money. I follow what my father did and what the county extension office advises.
